evidence: The diff adds no bare `except:`. The only new broad handler is src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:428, which is `except Exception:`. That does not catch KeyboardInterrupt or SystemExit, because both derive from BaseException and not Exception. It wraps safe_urlread(req).decode('utf-8') plus parse_qsl and falls back to payload={}, which then fails closed at :431 ('access_token' not in payload -> error page). Narrowing it to UnicodeDecodeError/ValueError would be a minor style choice. The premise of the comment is factually wrong.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:501-503 reads integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] directly. The 'sender' key is only added when state has it (:376-377, build_integration), and only the installation webhook supplies it (webhook.py:202-207). The Sentry-side pipeline state has no 'sender'. ensure_integration (integrations/pipeline.py:32-42) also overwrites metadata wholesale on update, so a pipeline install can remove a sender that the webhook stored earlier. Integrations created before this change, or whose metadata was overwritten this way, can therefore reach this branch (Integration exists, no OrganizationIntegration, e.g. after an uninstall from Sentry) and raise KeyError, which is a 500 instead of the error page. Fix: use integration.metadata.get('sender', {}).get('login') so a missing sender fails closed through error().

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:423 calls safe_urlopen outside the try block. The try at :426-429 only covers the read/parse. safe_urlopen (src/sentry/http.py:65-115) lets requests exceptions (ConnectionError, Timeout, SSLError, RestrictedIPAddress) propagate, so a network failure gives an unhandled 500 instead of error(). The comparable OAuth2CallbackView.exchange_token (src/sentry/identity/oauth2.py:286-308) catches SSLError and ConnectionError, which shows the codebase expects this handling. The impact is UX and noisy errors only: it fails closed, and RestrictedIPAddress or SuspiciousOperation are unrealistic for the fixed github.com URL. Moving the safe_urlopen call into the try, or catching requests.RequestException, would be enough.

src/sentry/identity/github/provider.py:7-17: get_user_info calls resp.raise_for_status() and resp.json() with no handling. The new call at src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:434 is unguarded, so a GitHub 4xx/5xx (rate limit, outage, revoked token) or a non-JSON body raises HTTPError or JSONDecodeError, which is a 500. The 'login' check at :435 only covers a well-formed response that lacks the key. Other callers (identity/github/provider.py:46, vsts, gitlab) also leave it unguarded, so this matches existing code. The token was just issued, so this is unlikely and fails closed. Wrapping the call in try/except and returning error() would be a cheap hardening.

In tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py the PR adds sequences like `resp = self.client.get(self.init_path_2)` followed immediately by `resp = self.client.get(self.setup_path_2)` (customer-domains test, ~L342-343 and ~L368-369 in the new file), and the same in test_github_user_mismatch, test_github_installed_on_another_org-style tests and the pending-deletion tests (~L698-711, ~L730-740). The test at ~L385 also leaves a now-unused `resp = self.client.get(...installation_id...)`. The first GET is still needed for its side effect (it binds pipeline state), but its return value is never read, so the assignment is dead (flake8/CodeQL 'unused local'). This is test-only cleanup: drop the `resp =` on the first call.
